static_traits.name: Zhang Yihang
static_traits.medical_history: No history of major physical illness; has not yet received psychotherapy in the past; no similar psychological problems before
static_traits.language_features: High cooperativeness, positive attitude, clear expression, able to self-reflect, coherent thinking

basic_info.main_problem: Because the new movie starring my favorite actor Robert De Niro did poorly at the box office, I feel I am a terrible fan, which makes me feel stressed and self-doubting.
basic_info.core_demands: I want to understand why I feel this way and find ways to cope with stress and self-doubt, to feel better and enjoy life again.

core_beliefs: I am a terrible (not loyal enough) fan
My worth depends on whether I can make my favorite actor's work successful

special_situations.event: Poor box office and mixed reviews after the movie's release
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my favorite actor's work fails, it means I am not loyal enough and have not fulfilled my duty of support
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Supports by going to movies, discussing with friends, and posting on social media, to prove one's loyalty
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all my fault; I am a bad fan; I let De Niro down

special_situations.event: Seeing negative reviews in the media or hearing others criticize the film
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others criticize the work, it means I have not done enough and am unqualified as a fan
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Pushing through by ignoring emotions and continuing daily life without dealing with them (push through)
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not good enough / not loyal enough; I should do more

special_situations.event: At work, thoughts drift to a movie's box office and reviews; attention is drawn to related information
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only if the film succeeds have I done my duty; otherwise I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly examines whether they have fulfilled their responsibilities as a fan, indulging in self-blaming thoughts
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I let him down; I am a failure

special_situations.event: When doing the originally enjoyed surfing activity, thinks of film performance and the mood drops
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: When the work is not successful, I am unworthy of enjoying life's pleasures
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing investment in interest activities, engaging in activities with guilt

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as a loyal, valued fan
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as disloyal or not good enough; worrying bad outcomes will be blamed on me
defense_goal: Maintaining loyalty and a sense of control through self-blame and self-demands, alleviating uncertainty and anxiety

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, a fan who may disappoint the idol

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When seeing bad reviews, poor box-office news, or hearing people talk about the film's performance
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equating external evaluations with negation of one's own loyalty; believing the film's failure is related to oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a self-blaming, low-key tone; frequently expressing in the pattern of 'I am not good enough / I should do more'; defending oneself less, actively taking responsibility and expressing guilt.

manifestations: Believes one should do more to support the film, and views box-office performance as a personal responsibility
When facing external criticism, increases self-restraint and sense of responsibility
outcomes: Hard to enjoy interest activities (e.g. surfing)

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Repeatedly using 'I should do more' to evaluate oneself
Directly equating the 'good fan' standard with whether the work can succeed

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Frequent self-doubt and self-blame (e.g., 'I am a bad fan')
In work and interest activities, occupied by inner self-criticism, hard to engage

positive_force: Able to identify and discuss automatic thoughts; willing to try alternative perspectives
Has already taken supportive actions (watching the film, discussing with friends, posting on social media)
Relatively stable work, with a basic life structure
negative_force: Cognitive biases of catastrophizing, personalization, overgeneralization, and 'should' statements
Binds self-worth to the success or failure of the idol's works, excessively seeking external validation
Highly sensitive to criticism, easily triggering guilt and self-doubt
High expectations leading to self-blame and low mood, affecting work and leisure

target_behavior.behavior: Intense self-blame and stress when facing negative reviews of a favorite actor's work
antecedent: Negative media reviews and others' criticism
Encountering news or discussions about the film's performance
target_behavior.core_reason: Personalizes external evaluation and demands of the self with 'should', binding loyalty to self-worth and seeking external validation
target_behavior.function: Escaping uncertainty and anxiety through self-blame and gaining a sense of control; maintaining a recognized loyal image
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood and worsening self-doubt; distraction at work; hard to enjoy interest activities (e.g., surfing)
